question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

$\frac{2}{25}\int_{10}^{40}\frac{{log}_{2}(2\left(\frac{x}{5}\right))}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡2$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\log_{2}\left(2 \left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\right).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\,⟹\,\ln{\left(2 \right)}\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $10$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{25}\int_{10}^{40}\frac{{log}_{2}(2\left(\frac{x}{5}\right))}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{25}\int_{10}^{40}{log}_{2}(2\left(\frac{x}{5}\right))\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\int_{2}^{4}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}2\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}{5}\int_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\operatorname{ln}2\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}\right)|_{2}^{4} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}2(16-4)\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left((6)\operatorname{ln}2\right)\end{aligned}
$$
